correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the unique radical decomposition; establishes five possible three-window local patterns and their exact probabilities; invokes the proved rational independence Lemma 2 in Narumi–Tachiya 2025; applies Kronecker–Weyl on each finite family and supplies an explicit summable scale-tail bound; classifies every exceptional radical <3; constructs positive-probability cylinder events for every supported triple; derives endpoint covariances from independent product moments and a Lipschitz Riemann sum. Checked actual standalone code for all 173 arithmetic triples (k=2 n=1..125, k=3 n=1..48), 100000 sampled phases per scale for six k values, and numerical large-k correction. Tests are finite corroboration, not the proof. No hidden empirical-moment convergence is claimed.

originality.rationale: The 2025 primary full text proves only one- and two-window densities, whereas this claim determines the genuine three-window coupling, nonzero same-radical endpoint pair contribution, the exact growing sharp support boundary and lag-two correlation gap. The two-window marginals alone cannot determine the three-way coupling; the original phase geometry establishes the added term. Verified primary paper and source metadata, searched accessible mathematical research records by statements and implications, not merely titles. Older literature might implicitly contain an equivalent multicylinder formula; this is recorded as priority risk.
residual_risks: Older 1980 and 2011 full primary texts were not exhaustively inspected, so an implicit general finite-cylinder framework may precede the 2025 paper.

value.rationale: Motivated k-full counting across consecutive k-th-power gaps; first nontrivial three-gap extension has a phase transition: one radical can populate both endpoints but never adjacent windows. That structure yields a linearly growing, pointwise sharp unavoidable count J_k, complete natural-density support for every triple, and a nonzero order-k difference of two covariance lags. Exact classification and positive density, not a narrow computation, establish value beyond known one-/two-window results.
